independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session 079e6503 (task T-DG7-REV-CS-R2). I verified the assignment's sha256, dac5d5fb…5d55. I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope.

Who authored what:
- P7 is by solution-architect, backend-workflow-engineer, kpi-benefits-engineer, frontend-ux-engineer, transformation-analyst and devops-engineer (docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/).
- The acceptance suites are by qa-verifier.
- The drills, host runs and freeze are by the delivery-orchestrator.
- The round-1 repairs: FE-C2, FE-C3, BE-R6, DO-K2, AN-P7E, and the orchestrator's environment.md and progress.md edits.

My round-1 run was BLOCKED at the identity check (F-DG7-953 records why), so this is my first product review of DG7. None of the six findings I verify here is mine, and I authored none of their fixes.

My only writes are:
- evidence under docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/code-security/round-2/;
- my three round-2 review files, written with the Write tool.
Every build, test, probe and mutant ran in a disposable --shared sparse clone under $TMPDIR with a disposable PostgreSQL. The clone was removed at the end (90-cleanup.log). Validators and register checks ran read-only on the live repository.

I formed this verdict before reading any other reviewer's round-2 record. During my run, HEAD moved to 98c4e94bb, the domain reviewer's auto-committed round-2 records. I recorded only the file names (42-head-moved.log) and did not open them. I read the round-1 records of the other reviewers, which belong to a different round, only for the finding texts and the register context.

The assignment says 'round: 7'. The validator (tools/gates/lib/rules.mjs l.682, l.794) requires rec.round to equal the round directory, so I record round 2. This contradiction in the assignment is reported here.

checks_run.procedure: Recompute the candidate on the working tree, at HEAD and at the source commit, and diff it against the frozen manifest.
checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7 [--ref HEAD | --ref f22c97b59 | --diff docs/delivery/candidates/DG7/ca38b65ecaa23f49.manifest.json]
checks_run.expected: The candidate ID is sha256:ca38b65e…13c5 over 3153 files. HEAD equals the source, or is a freeze commit that touches only META-excluded files.
checks_run.actual:
HEAD is abc7254f6, the round-2 freeze commit and the direct child of the source f22c97b59. It changes only the 3 assignments, the manifest and stages.json, all META-excluded; decisions.md is untouched. The working tree, --ref HEAD and --ref f22c97b59 each give sha256:ca38b65ecaa23f49b4e5755f503c88e74c3a5bd502862fd28cc5ddbbd1fe13c5 over 3153 files, exit 0. --diff reports matches: true with nothing added, removed or changed.

This matches the DG5 and DG6 precedent: HEAD is the freeze commit on top of the source. That is why I did not stop here, unlike round 1.

HEAD later moved to 98c4e94bb (domain records); the candidate there is still ca38b65e (42-head-moved.log). There are no errors in the logs.

checks_run.procedure: Review the source of apps/api/src/modules/transfer/config-bundle/{routes,service,plan,registry}.ts, the four kind adapters (methodology, admin, jobs, tasks) and packages/shared/src/transfer/config-bundle.ts. Check authorization, validation, If-Match, locks, audit, size limits, unportable references and secrets.
checks_run.expected: Every mutation has server-side authorization (re-checked in the transaction), validation, optimistic concurrency and an audit event. config_bundle.import never widens a right. Nothing is published.
checks_run.actual:
Met; no defect found.

Authorization:
- config_bundle.export/import is checked at the named organization (requireRightAt) and re-checked on grants reloaded inside each mutation's transaction (freshRightAt + commitTimeDenial).
- Each kind's own configure right is checked at plan time (adapter.permitted) and again at write time by the adapters. The checks equal the existing routes' own-organization checks (requireStudioPermission, requireInOwnOrganization).
- M2 proves the per-kind test detects a bypass.
- AUD and no-grant users get 403 on all nine operations (test l.677).

Integrity:
- validate and commit take If-Match, the configBundleImport advisory lock, FOR UPDATE and a versioned UPDATE.
- commit re-plans and refuses plan_changed with nothing written.
- Each item is written through its kind's path with its own audit event.
- An import never publishes: drafts go through review, and job schedules end disabled.

Upload:
- size: declared above 5 MiB is 413 before the body is read; a streamed oversize is mapped to 413.
- the version is checked first, then checksums and per-kind schemas; duplicate keys are refused.
- the stored bytes are canonical, and SHA-256 is re-checked on read and download.

Other:
- the object store uses confinedPath, which refuses '..' and absolute paths.
- Content-Disposition uses only the row uuid.
- no kind schema carries a secret.
- automation_rule is refused explicitly (ADR-0065 Amendment 1, disclosed).

Observations, not defects:
- GET by id answers 404 before the organization check, an existence oracle of uuid v7 ids to holders of the right elsewhere; the codebase's ADR-0006 pattern does the same.
- The X-File-Name header is reduced to printable ASCII (ui.tsx l.149), so an Arabic file name is stored as underscores. That is cosmetic; the contract allows only a header string.

checks_run.procedure: Review the source of packages/db/src/transfer/{import,export,plan,rebind,manifest}.ts, the migration API routes (export, import read views, attachments), tools/migration/*.mjs and migrations 0133 to 0152. Check the audit append-only handling, the trust boundary, injection and credentials.
checks_run.expected: audit_event is never updated, deleted or truncated, and its triggers are never disabled. Credential tables are never exported. Dynamic SQL is catalogue-driven and quoted. Paths are confined. The rebind is all-or-nothing, optimistic and audited.
checks_run.actual:
Met; no defect found.

import.ts:
- The load runs in one transaction under LOCK TABLE audit_event IN EXCLUSIVE MODE.
- It disables USER triggers only on the other exported tables (quoteIdent) and asserts that both audit_event triggers stay enabled ('O').
- It never DELETEs or TRUNCATEs audit_event.
- The plan comes from the TARGET's catalogue and must equal the package's table and column lists.
- E1 refuses a target holding non-baseline audit rows.
- Every package file is SHA-256-checked through confinedPath; --manifest-sha256 lets IT pin the manifest.
- The package is not signed. The trust boundary is the IT operator with the owner role, as ADR-0064 states.

Plan and export:
- Unlisted tables are exported by default (deny-by-exception), and session, oidc_login_state and idempotency_record are excluded as credential or operational.
- The migration API exposes manifests only: no row values, no evidence bytes. It needs migration.export at organization scope, with an Idempotency-Key and an audit event.

rebind.ts:
- It validates every line under the identityRebind lock before any write.
- Each hold is updated with a versioned update, with one identity_rebind_event and one audit event per hold.
- A user not in the file stays unbound and cannot sign in; M3 proves that test detects a bypass.

Other:
- dry-run.ts quotes its database names and refuses a production-marked copy without the confirm flag.
- The P7 integration files (transfer-load, roundtrip, recheck, locks, guards, catalogue) all passed in check 05.

checks_run.procedure: Review the source of the retention routes and services, the worker job retention.archive, migrations 0143, 0144 and 0148 (SECURITY DEFINER purge), and backup.sh, restore.sh and the compose backup profile.
checks_run.expected: Only past-retention operational records can be purged, through one guarded path. Every action is audited. Business, audit and snapshot records are never purged. The scripts are injection-safe.

checks_run.procedure: Review the D-258 item 2 OIDC loopback exception (packages/config load.ts secureIssuerAllowed, identity/oidc.ts allowHttp) and the identity_unbound refusal in the OIDC and dev logins.
checks_run.environment: Live repository source at f22c97b59 (read); unit and integration results from checks 04-06
checks_run.expected: In production a plain-http issuer is accepted only on an exact loopback host. Every other plain-http issuer is refused by the loader. An unbound carried user cannot sign in by any path.
checks_run.actual:
Met.

isLoopbackHost is an exact set membership (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]), so a host such as 'localhost.evil' does not match. The loader refuses any other plain-http issuer in production. allowHttp follows the same rule, and oidc-allow-http.test.ts covers both sides (unit-node passed).

identity_unbound is checked for an existing identity, for e-mail binding and for the dev login, and each refusal is audited. M3 detects removing the first check.

Observation, not a defect: openid-client's allowHttp applies to every endpoint the loopback issuer's discovery document names, so a misconfigured loopback drill IdP could advertise a plain-http non-loopback token endpoint. The issuer itself is IT-controlled and local by construction (drill only; D-258), so I do not raise it.

checks_run.procedure: Review the secret scanner rules and the allow-list loader (DO-J2), secret-allowlist.json (46 entries), asset-scan-allowlist.json (DO-E6) and gate-labels-acknowledged.json (ADR-0073 §6, flagged for code-security in D-268). Check that tools/gates, tools/agents and .claude/agents are unchanged since the DG6 approval.
checks_run.environment: Live repository source at f22c97b59 (read); self-tests from check 09
checks_run.expected: No entry can hide a real secret or a broad class. Protected paths cannot be allow-listed. Acknowledgements are bound to exact sentences of approved DG0-DG6 records. The gate tooling cannot be weakened.
checks_run.actual:
Met.

Secret allow-list:
- Entries match rule, path and the value's SHA-256; no value is stored.
- The loader refuses entries covering .env.example, deploy/compose|docker|keycloak/**, docs/handover/** and non-test src/**, and a stale entry fails the scan.
- The docs/delivery/** entries are scoped to history and envelope and to specific value hashes.

Asset allow-list: only R4 documentation hosts appear inside bundled third-party text. The loader refuses R1, R3 and R5 in T1 and T2.

Acknowledgements: there is one entry (L3, DG3.json $.notes, sentence sha256). The loader accepts only L3 and L4 and only ^docs/delivery/gates/DG[0-6].json$; DG7, the README and the final report can never be acknowledged.

Gate tooling: git diff 944aaf810..f22c97b59 shows no change to tools/gates, tools/agents or .claude/agents.

Observation: S3's SYNTHETIC_MARKER treats any value containing 'example', 'dummy' or 'placeholder' as a non-secret. This is a documented heuristic (ADR-0063 §5 residual 1). S1 and S2 do not honour it.

checks_run.procedure: Review the source of deploy/docker/Dockerfile (DO-E3: every workspace manifest copied, corepack into PNPM_HOME), assemble-runtime.sh (pnpm metadata stripped, virtual-store check), image-bundle.sh (DO-E4) and tools/release/{seal,verify-seal}.mjs.
checks_run.environment: Live repository source at f22c97b59 (read); self-tests from check 09
checks_run.expected: There are no public-CDN or builder-hosted runtime dependencies and no secret in an image. Loaded images are integrity-checked. The verify-seal checks cannot be passed vacuously.
checks_run.actual:
Met; no defect found.

Dockerfile: the build CA comes in as a BuildKit secret, never as a layer. The new COPY of packages/reporting/package.json is test-pinned (dockerfile-context.test.mjs, in the orchestrator's deploy-tool run).

assemble-runtime.sh: it removes .modules.yaml, the workspace-state file and .bin shims, which carry build-host paths, and asserts they are gone.

image-bundle.sh:
- It checks the tar's SHA-256 against images.json before docker load.
- It requires the containerd store, so the digest pins resolve.
- It never pulls, pushes or re-tags on the target.
- images.json and the tar travel together, so that check guards corruption. Substitution is guarded by Compose's digest-pinned image: lines, which are unchanged.

verify-seal reads the envelope in memory (no extraction) and checks paths with isSafeRelPath. It reports BLOCKED, never PASS, for a check that could not run. REHEARSAL-PASS never counts as A28. The seal and verify-seal self-tests passed in check 09.

checks_run.procedure: Judge the orchestrator's container-host evidence for D-267. I did NOT re-run it: there is no Docker daemon in this sandbox. The evidence is the host runs (image build, bundle save/load, no-egress stack, Keycloak e2e outside the build proxy).
checks_run.expected: The final host run passes, every earlier failure is disclosed, and the limits are stated.
checks_run.actual:
This check is a reading of evidence, not a container run of mine.

host-run.log (run 1) shows the Keycloak e2e failing 4 tests with ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED (step 11 exit=1). D-267/D-268 disclose this: the build proxy intercepted the e2e process, and the earlier runs host-run-1 (image build failed) and host-run-2 (bundle names lost) are kept. host-run-3c.log runs the Keycloak e2e with the proxy variables unset (b07): 4 passed, exit 0; b05, b06 and b08 exit 0.

keycloak-e2e-stack.log's 'unexpected iss' ClientError lines are the wrong-issuer negative test (/login?error=token_invalid). The 'logical replication launcher exited with exit code 1' lines are routine PostgreSQL shutdown messages.

The disclosed limits stand: one host, not air-gapped, not HA. I accept the evidence as the orchestrator's, with those residuals. My own result here covers only this reading.

summary:
FAIL on candidate ca38b65e because of one new finding, F-DG7-935 (Medium, blocking, not mandatory). The frozen register has 18 DG7-final rows SPECIFIED, and requirements.csv is a candidate file. validate --register DG7 exits 1 with 18 problems, and validateGate runs that rule, so this candidate cannot validate as an approved DG7. D-266 (d)'s 'the release-auditor decides at the gate' is not possible under the validator. Read literally, these 18 requirements are not met; the other 36 are met.

I found no security, authorization, integrity or injection defect in the P7 code I reviewed (config bundle, migration import, export, rebind and audit, retention purge, OIDC loopback, scanners and allow-lists, Dockerfile and image bundle, seal and verify).

What I ran: typecheck, lint, openapi lint, no-CDN, unit, the 47-file P7 integration subset, Retention e2e in AR and EN, security tooling self-tests, payload and history secret scans, claims scan and validators. All pass after re-runs: the typecheck OOM, the ENOSPC file, the sparse-clone artefact and the run 1 web timeouts are each disclosed. Four authorization mutants are each killed.

All six round-1 findings (913, 914, 953, 954, 955, 956) are CLOSED_VERIFIED. No business, Finance or IT approval is implied, and product G6 does not imply DG7.
